Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:42: And when a person drinks water for his thirst, he must direct this intention, to remember God's miracles for our people. And specifically "for his thirst," because when a person is thirsty, his stomach is inflamed with fire, and this indicates judgment; and in his drinking the water, it indicates that they are the waters of Chesed that extinguish the judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:43: And so too, the blessing "who creates many souls" is literally this same intention, of remembering the miracles of Chesed - except that the blessing "shehakol" is general and "who creates souls" is particular; and the intent of "who creates souls and their deficiencies" is that this creation is from the side of Chesed, for He creates what the souls need - namely, sufficient provision, for the world cannot endure except through them, along the lines of water, which is the life of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:44: And in the first blessing, the term "nihyah" [came to be] is used, and here "beriah" [creation] - these two actions are related to Chesed. "Yad-vav" [an allusion, YHV, of the tetragrammaton's first three letters] is like "let there be light" (Genesis 1:3). And likewise "creation" - it is known what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 133a), "Adam of Beriah rides upon the lion"; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:45: "For everything He created, to give life through them to the soul of every living thing" - "for everything" - although it is explained that the miracles come from the side of Chesed, the intent is that they are revealed in Chesed, and Chesed is in the Righteous One [Tzaddik/Yesod], but their true source is higher above - and the proof is the splitting of the Red Sea, which is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach, page 52b) to depend on the Atika [Ancient One]. And therefore, after mentioning what He created for the sake of Chesed - namely, the sustenance without which existence is impossible - it says afterward the matter of performing the miracles, which are higher above and are revealed within the waters of Chesed - and this is "for everything He created, to give life."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:46: And this is what the author of the discourse began with, saying that all the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel were performed only concerning water - meaning, the place of their revelation is in water - and therefore the first plague was concerning water, to show that all the other miracles to be performed would be revealed through it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:47: And it says "for everything He created," using the term "al" [for/upon], similar to (Isaiah 58:14), "then you shall delight yourself upon [al] the LORD" - which is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Yitro, page 83a) - and "al HaShem" is literally "al Kol Mah" [upon "Kol Mah," an anagram/allusion] - meaning, from what is above "Kol Mah," from there He created to give life to the soul of every living thing - for from there comes the life that gives being to souls. And because the matter is in a concealed place, it does not say "for what You create to give life," which would be a continually occurring action, but rather "what He created" - concealed above, in the hidden place, "Adam of Beriah" of the supernal.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:48: And within this several things are included. The first, what the commentators explain, that "to give life to the soul of every living thing" refers to the extra pleasures, for it is from there that they flow, as it says, "you shall delight yourself upon the LORD." And so too the miracles that are life for Israel come from there. And "the soul of every living thing" over whom death rules are given life through the supernal flow. This also includes the delight of souls - the souls of the righteous in the World to Come, for each of the righteous is called "living," as it is said (II Samuel 23:20), "and Benaiah son of Yehoyada, son of a living man" - and this is "to give life to the soul of every living thing."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:49: And this blessing was instituted specifically over water, because when a person remembers the constantly occurring lower Chesed - which is the water, or the other things of pleasure that a person eats, all of which are included in the category of lower Chesed - he will then remember the supernal Chesed that the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to perform - and this is "for everything He created" - explained as the wondrous pleasure that is there, and likewise what He has already done concerning the matter of miracles; and through this he cleaves to His love properly.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:50: And at the end of the blessing, when we say "blessed is the Life of the worlds," this may be understood through what Rashbi, peace be upon him, says (Zohar, Parashat Toldot Yitzchak, end of page 135), concerning the matter of the righteous one being called "the Life of the worlds"; he says there, in these words: he is "chai" [living] in two worlds - above, which is the supernal world, [he is] "chai" toward the lower world, and the lower world exists and shines for his sake - to this point. And it is possible to say that the two kinds of flow we mentioned - one, the flow of sustenance, and the second, the flow of pleasure and miracles - are the two worlds explained in the discourse; and understand this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:51: Further, what showed us His love, blessed be He, was the descent of the manna, as it says in Tanchuma (Beshalach, Buber edition), on the verse (Exodus 16:4), "behold, I will rain bread for you" - this is what Scripture says (Job 36:31), "for by them He judges the peoples; He gives food in abundance." "By them" - by these heavens He judges the nations of the world - know this: when the generation of the Flood sinned, He judged them by them, as it is said (Psalms 11:6), "He shall rain snares upon the wicked." When the men of Sodom sinned, He judged them with the heavens, as it is said (Genesis 19:24), "and the LORD rained upon Sodom," and so on. When Sisera sinned, He judged him with the heavens, as it is said (Judges 5:20), "they fought from heaven." "He gives food in abundance" - from them He gave food to Israel, as it is said (Exodus 16:4), "behold, I will rain bread for you from heaven." A parable: to what may this be compared? To a baker who stood by the furnace; his enemy came in, and he scooped up the coals and put them on his head; his beloved came in, and he took out warm bread and gave it to him - the coals and the bread both came out of the same furnace. So the Holy One, blessed be He, brought down fire on the people of Sodom and burned them, and from the heavens He brought down manna for Israel - to the extent relevant here. And they further elaborate there on several miracles performed with the manna, and this is enough to arouse the heart in love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:52: Further, what showed the Holy One, blessed be He's love for us was the giving of the Torah, as it says (Exodus 19:4), "you have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to Myself. Now therefore, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be a treasured possession [segulah] to Me from among all peoples, for all the earth is Mine." And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain in the Mechilta: "and you shall be a treasured possession to Me from among all peoples" - that you shall be free for Me and occupy yourselves with My words of Torah, and not be occupied with other matters. "Segulah" - just as a person's treasure [segulah] is precious to him, so you shall be precious to Me. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Karchah says: so that it be firmly fixed in your ear - just as a wife is devoted [misgelet] to her husband, and a son to his father, and a servant to his master, and a maidservant to her mistress - might you think you too are so devoted [to others]? The verse teaches, "for all the earth is Mine" - and you shall be to Me, as it were, I appoint and empower none over you but Myself, and so it says (Psalms 121:4), "behold, He who keeps Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps." "A kingdom of priests" - I appoint no king over you from the nations of the world; and so it says (Song of Songs 6:9), "my dove is unique" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:53: And the discourse of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Karchah is understood together with what Rashi explains on this verse, in these words: "segulah" - a beloved treasury, like "and the treasure [segulat] of kings," precious vessels and gems that kings store away - so you shall be to Me a treasure above the other nations; and do not say, you alone are Mine and I have no others with you, so what more is there, that your affection should be distinguished to Me, since "all the earth is Mine," and they [the other nations] are as nothing before Me? - rather, "and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests," princes, as it says (II Samuel 8:18), "and David's sons were priests."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:54: And He showed us the matter of love when He said "and you shall be to Me," and they explain, of blessed memory, "I appoint none to rule over you but Myself." And along these lines Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar, Vayikra, page 7b), in these words: happy is Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, did not give them over to a prince or a messenger, but rather Israel hold onto Him and He holds onto them; and out of His affection for them, the Holy One, blessed be He, called them servants - this is what is written (Leviticus 25:55), "for the children of Israel are servants to Me; they are My servants" - afterward He called them children, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children of the LORD your God" - afterward He called them brothers, as it is written (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and my friends" - because He called them "My brothers," He wished to make His dwelling among them and not depart from them - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:55: And so too, concerning the matter of the love shown in the Torah, Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, rebuked us in Deuteronomy (Deuteronomy 4:32), "for ask now of the former days... whether there has been any such great thing as this, or has anything been heard like it? Did a people ever hear the voice of God," and so on; and it says (ibid. 4:36), "out of heaven He made you hear His voice, that He might instruct you; and upon earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire. And because He loved your fathers, therefore He chose their descendants after them, and brought you out with His presence, with His mighty power, out of Egypt."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:56: And along these lines, concerning the matter of love in the giving of the Torah to us (ibid. 4:38), "to drive out nations from before you greater and mightier than you, to bring you in, to give you their land for an inheritance, as it is this day."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:57: And concerning His love for us in the giving of the Torah, see what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Parashat Balak, page 192a), on the verse (Deuteronomy 33:2), "the LORD came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir," and so on - from there is shown the strength of His love, blessed be He, for us, like a father who loves his beloved son.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:58: And of this aspect of love in the giving of the Torah, it says in the Mishnah (Avot 3:14): beloved are Israel, for they were given the precious instrument through which the world was created, as it is said (Proverbs 4:2), "for I give you good doctrine," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:59: And concerning the general category of miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for us, we say in the Haggadah of Passover night: "how much more so, then, is the doubled and redoubled goodness of the Omnipresent upon us! He brought us out of Egypt, executed judgments upon them, executed judgment on their gods, killed their firstborn, gave us their wealth, split the sea for us, brought us through it on dry land, sank our enemies in it, provided for our needs in the wilderness for forty years, fed us the manna, gave us the Shabbat, brought us before Mount Sinai, gave us the Torah, brought us into the land of Israel, and built us the Chosen House [Temple] to atone for all our sins."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:60: And so too, among the things showing the Holy One, blessed be He's love for Israel, is when a person considers the order of prayer that the Men of the Great Assembly instituted for us - one of them being what we say every day in prayer, "with everlasting love You have loved us, O LORD our God; great and abundant mercy You have shown us." And several particulars are mentioned in it indicating His great love for us, and were we to elaborate on it we would depart from our intent. In general, they are: (1) "great and abundant mercy You have shown us" - and this is the general category for all the particular aspects that will be explained in the blessing. (1) "Our Father, for the sake of Your great Name" - meaning, that shared with us. (2) "for the sake of our fathers who trusted in You." (3) "and You taught them the statutes of life." (4) "our Father, merciful Father, have mercy upon us." (5) "and put understanding in our hearts" - for He has given us intellect to understand more than the other nations. (6) "that we shall not be ashamed, nor confounded, nor stumble forever and ever" - meaning, for the world that is entirely long. (7) "we shall rejoice and be glad in Your salvation" - namely, "I am with him in distress" (Psalms 91:15). (8) "and break the yoke of the nations from off our neck" - meaning, the ingathering of the exiles. (9) "for You are a God who works salvations" - for He always performs salvations for the sustaining of the world, and these are the five salvations explained in the Zohar at the beginning of Parashat Bereshit (1a), and further in Parashat Terumah. (10) "and You have chosen us from among every people and tongue" - meaning (Deuteronomy 32:8), "when the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when He separated the sons of man... for the LORD's portion is His people." (11) "and You have brought us near, our King, to Your great Name" - I heard from the mouth of my teacher, the honorable Rabbi Yitzchak de Luria Ashkenazi, that one should have in mind here that He brought us near to His Name at the standing at Mount Sinai, to give us the Torah - for the Torah and His great Name are entirely one, as explained in the Zohar in several places. (12) "to give thanks to You." (13) "to proclaim Your unity and to love [You]" - for "ahavah" [love] adds up [in gematria] to "echad" [one] - and these are the thirteen kinds of love mentioned in this blessing, corresponding to the numerical value of "ahavah."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:61: And so too, among the things that arouse love, we mention in the blessing "Emet VeYatziv" [True and Firm]: "God of the world, our King, Rock of Jacob, Shield of our salvation, from generation to generation; true it is that You are the LORD our God and the God of our fathers, our King, the King of our fathers, our Redeemer, the Redeemer of our fathers, our Rock, the Rock of our salvation," and so on, "help of our fathers, You are He from of old, a Shield and Savior to them and their children after them" - and from here on, all the matters, all of them, until "the LORD, Redeemer of Israel" - all of it indicates the Holy One, blessed be He's love for us, and His performing several miracles, such as the Exodus from Egypt, the plague of the firstborn, the splitting of the Sea, and the other particulars mentioned - that if a person takes this to heart in reciting the blessing, and does not recite it as "a commandment of men, learned by rote," his heart will certainly be aroused with great desire and love for the Holy One, blessed be He, and he will cleave to Him while standing and praying before Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:62: And so too, in the blessing "Magen Avraham" [Shield of Abraham], which hints at Chesed - everything we mention in it is kindnesses and acts of Chesed that arouse love: "God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob" - and this distinction we have already mentioned above, that it is the matter of (Deuteronomy 10:15), "only in your fathers did the LORD delight, to love them," and so on, as explained above. "The great God, the supernal God, who bestows good kindnesses, who acquires everything, and remembers the kindnesses of the fathers, and brings a redeemer," and so on - and all these actions indicate the constancy of Chesed among creatures without interruption; for it does not say "bestowed kindnesses" but "bestows" - that He always bestows; and likewise "acquires everything" - it does not say "acquired everything," "and remembered My kindnesses," and "brought a redeemer," but rather "acquires," "remembers," and "brings" - which certainly indicates the constancy of the acts of Chesed. And in the commentary on the prayer, every single one of these actions will be explained, how it indicates Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:63: And so too, in the blessing "Atah Gibor" [You Are Mighty] - although it resembles Gevurah, it is the sweetened Gevurah bound to Chesed, for we see that all the workings of Chesed are mentioned in it: "who revives the dead," "who sustains the living with kindness, revives the dead with abundant mercy, supports the falling, and heals the sick, and releases the bound, and keeps His faith" - and the matter of judgment is not explicitly mentioned except in the word "King, who brings death," and immediately after it He says "and gives life" - for even the matter of death, which is the harshest judgment, His intent, blessed be He, is for the good of man, in order to give him life, so that the world go forth from its curses - for then the LORD will rejoice in His works. And the particulars of its matters, mentioned several times, of death and their other functions, will be explained in the matter of prayer. It follows that this blessing is Gevurah bound to Chesed, and so it is along the lines of what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Ki Tisa, page 190b), which we copied in chapter 1 of this Gate: that Abraham loves Isaac and Isaac loves Abraham, embracing one another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:64: Further, what we mention in the "Modim" blessing: "for our lives, which are committed into Your hand, and for our souls, which are entrusted to You, and for Your miracles which are with us every day - [You who are] good, for Your mercies never cease." And what we mention after our prayers, the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, "God, merciful and gracious," and so on, which indicate great kindness to every person - let him examine these carefully. And so too what we say on the Shabbat day, "and had our mouths been full of song as the sea," and so on, "of old, from Egypt, You redeemed us, O LORD our God; therefore the limbs You have apportioned within us, and the spirit and soul You have breathed into our nostrils, and the tongue You have set in our mouths," and so on, "who saves the poor from one stronger than he; the cry of the poor You hear."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:65: And so too what we say in the Grace after Meals, in the blessing "Nodeh" [We Thank]: "for having given as an inheritance to our fathers a desirable, good land," and so on, "for having brought us out of the land of Egypt, for Your covenant which You have sealed in our flesh" - and this indicates the bond of love, that He, blessed be He, is bound with us, since the sign of His Name is sealed in our flesh; and so it is the way of friends who love one another to make a binding sign between them, as a token of love that will never be forgotten. "For Your Torah which You have taught us" - explained above. And the matter of food is also from the token of His kindness to all creatures.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:66: And so too, when a person remembers how many miracles were performed through the prophets - some through Samuel, some through Elijah, some through Elisha - he will recognize His greatness and His goodness toward Israel. And besides this, the miracles performed for Israel in every single generation, which, were we to come to recount them, no book could contain - and this is what we say, that in every single generation, the idol-worshipping nations rise up against us to destroy us, and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves us from their hand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:67: And the general category of miracles we have written, and several more that we have not mentioned, are all mentioned in the book of Ezra [Nehemiah] (Nehemiah 9:6-28): "You alone are the LORD; You have made the heavens," and so on; "You are the LORD, the God who chose Abram," and so on; "and You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt," and so on; "and You divided the sea before them," and so on; "and with a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and with a pillar of fire by night, to give them light," and so on; "and You came down upon Mount Sinai, and spoke with them from heaven, and gave them right ordinances," and so on; "and made known to them Your holy Sabbath," and so on; "and gave them bread from heaven for their hunger, and brought forth water for them out of the rock for their thirst; and You told them to go in to possess the land," and so on; "but they and our fathers dealt proudly, and hardened their necks," and so on; "but You are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and did not forsake them - even when they made themselves a molten calf," and so on; "yet You, in Your abundant mercies, did not forsake them in the wilderness; the pillar of cloud did not depart from over them by day," and so on; "and You gave Your good spirit to instruct them, and did not withhold Your manna from their mouth," and so on; "forty years You sustained them in the wilderness; their garments did not wear out," and so on; "and You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and divided them into portions; and their children You multiplied as the stars of heaven," and so on; "and they captured fortified cities and a fat land, and possessed houses full of every good thing," and so on; "yet they were disobedient and rebelled against You," and so on; "therefore You delivered them into the hand of their adversaries, who distressed them; and in the time of their distress, they cried to You, and You heard from heaven, and in Your abundant mercies You gave them saviors," and so on; "but as soon as they had rest, they returned to do evil before You; therefore You abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, who ruled over them; then they returned and cried out to You, and You heard from heaven and delivered them, many times, according to Your mercies." And so it is said in the book of Judges (Judges 10:16), "and His soul was grieved for the misery of Israel" - see how great His affection is for us, like a person distressed over his son's suffering.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:68: And further, there in Ezra [Nehemiah] (9:30-31): "and You bore with them many years, and testified against them by Your spirit, through Your prophets; yet they would not give ear," and so on; "and in Your abundant mercies You did not make an end of them, nor forsake them, for You are a gracious and merciful God" - to this point, in the book of Ezra.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:69: Further, one should discern what our Rabbis say in tractate Avot (5:5): ten miracles were performed for our fathers in the Temple - "no woman miscarried [because of the smell of the sacrificial meat]," and so on. And this, when the Temple stood, was a sign for Israel that the Shechinah dwelt among us - and as the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz writes on the Mishnah "shame of face [leads] to the Garden of Eden" (see there, mishnah 20): may it be [His] will that the Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:70: And just as the Tabernacle is called "the Tabernacle of Testimony," being a testimony to Israel that the Shechinah rested among them, so too this was true of the Temple, through the working of miracles that were in it - particularly on Yom Kippur, with the crimson-colored thread that would turn white, to indicate whether "though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow" (Isaiah 1:18).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:71: And even now, that it is destroyed, it is a sign that this is because of our sins, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to build the Temple with His own hands - for when Israel left Egypt, His intent, blessed be He, was to bring down for us the Temple built above, had they not sinned with the calf. And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 221a), in these words: when Israel left Egypt, the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to make them like holy angels above, on earth, and He wished to build them a holy house and bring it down from the heavens of the firmaments, and to plant Israel a holy planting in the manner of the supernal image - this is what is written (Exodus 15:17), "You shall bring them in and plant them in the mountain of Your inheritance, the place, O LORD, which You have made for Your dwelling" - in that which You made, O LORD, and no other - "the place for Your dwelling which You have made" - this is the First Temple; "the sanctuary, O LORD, which Your hands have established" - this is the Second Temple; and both of them are the craftsmanship of the Holy One, blessed be He. And since they angered Him in the wilderness, they died, and the Holy One, blessed be He, gathered them to build it in the land, from the fruit of their own deeds, and the house was built by the hand of man, and therefore it did not endure - to this point. And they further elaborate there on this exposition; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:72: And so too, the miracle performed for all Israel in the days of Mordechai and Esther was an endorsement for the whole Torah, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Shabbat, chapter "Perek Arvei Pesachim" [chapter 9], page 88a): for at first the mountain was forced over them like a barrel, which is a great objection against the [voluntariness of the] Torah - but in the days of Haman, "they confirmed and accepted" (Esther 9:27) - they confirmed what they had already accepted - meaning, they confirmed with willingness and love what they had accepted under compulsion, because they saw how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for them, like a father having compassion on his son, whom the son is obligated to perform his father's will.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:73: And you must know that all the miracles performed for us, and what is performed every day, and what will be performed, all comes through the Shechinah bound with us, who is the merciful Mother - and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 17b): and because she is imprisoned with them in exile, it is said of her, "there is no prisoner who releases himself from prison" - and the Shechinah is in his own prison house, for out of her love for him she is imprisoned within it - and the secret of the matter is (Song of Songs 1:13), "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, lodging between my breasts" - and therefore whoever wishes to approach the King has no permission to approach Him except through the Shechinah - this is what is written (Jeremiah 9:22), "let not the wise man glory," and so on, "but only in this" - and Aaron, when he entered the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur, entered through her, as it is written (Leviticus 16:3), "with this [bezot] shall Aaron come into the holy place" - for she is "a time to act for the LORD" [an allusion to "zot" and the sefirah of Malchut]. And Moses endured in the world for her sake - this is what is written (Deuteronomy 33:1), "and this [vezot] is the blessing with which [Moses] blessed." And through her he performed the ten plagues upon Pharaoh - this is what is written (Exodus 9:16), "and indeed for this cause [ba'avur zot] I have raised you up." And Jacob, because he knew that all the King's desire is [directed] through her, instructed his sons that they should approach before the King only through her, and all their requests, in their prayers and supplications to the King, should be through her - this is what is written (Genesis 49:28), "and this [vezot] is what their father spoke to them." And David, because he knew that all the King's desire, strength, and might are through her, said (Psalms 27:3), "though [a camp] should encamp against me," and so on, "in this [bezot] I am confident" - of which it is said (Psalms 103:19), "and His kingdom rules over all." And therefore, when Israel seek requests from the King, they say to her (Song of Songs 6:1), "where has your beloved turned aside? That we may seek him with you" - with several requests of prayers and supplications - for it is for your sake that he descends to us; he has not departed from us except because we do not give you honor, for it is for your sake that he was imprisoned with us all six [weekday] days - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that the ten plagues were performed through her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:74: And so too, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Parashat Ha'azinu, page 296b), concerning the matter of (Deuteronomy 32:6), "do you thus repay [tigmelu zot] the LORD?" - in these words: Rabbi Yehuda said, "do you thus repay the LORD" - because you are a perverse and crooked generation, you caused this ["zot"] to be exiled in exile - "do you thus repay the LORD" - this is the repayment you make Him, for all those laws of Egypt, all those signs He performed for you - this is the repayment you complete for this! Who caused this to you? Because you are a foolish and unwise people, and you do not consider all the good He has done for you until now. "Do you thus repay the LORD" - "zot" is the Shechinah, and we have already established this matter - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:75: And so too he explains in Shemot Rabbah, Parashat "Vayisa Moshe," and so on (24:1), on this verse, and mentions the miracles there; and it appears from there that the two heh's, Imma Ila'ah and Imma Tata'ah, both participated in performing the miracles; in these words: "and Moses caused Israel to journey" - this is what is written, "do you thus repay the LORD" - Rabbi Shisha, son of Rabbi Abba, would write the heh below and the lamed above [in a special orthography], meaning "hoy" [woe] - "do you thus repay the LORD, after all the miracles He performed for you" - that He split the sea for you into twelve pieces, and sank the Egyptians in the sea, His hand sinking them while His other hand saved you, as it is said (Exodus 15:6), "Your right hand, O LORD, is glorious in power; Your right hand, O LORD," and so on - and He brought you up from the sea, and gave you their silver and gold, and everything that was on their horses, adorned with silver and gold; and He sustained you for forty years, and did not leave you even one hour - how many enemies came upon you, and He did not let you flee, but rather cast them down before you and protected you - and not only from your enemies, but even from snakes and scorpions - and He gave you light before you, as it is said (Exodus 13:21), "and the LORD went before them by day." You have forgotten all these miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed with you, and the image of Micah passed with you, and you abandoned words of Torah and occupied yourselves with other matters - this is what is written "do you thus repay the LORD" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:76: And therefore it is fitting that we not be ungrateful for the goodness and kindnesses we have received from Him, blessed be He, but rather strive to perform His will and love Him just as He loves us; and we arouse the reality of this love in our prayer and our commandments, to unify the Shechinah - and every unification is love, as explained above - and this is "and you shall love the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 6:5). And particularly in this exile of ours, where the unity is separated and our Mother is in exile because of our sins - as it says (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother is sent away" - we must repair the unity through our prayer and commandments, and it is like the parable of a son who loves his mother, that he should ask his father for the rest of her clothing and answer his impoverished mother, and complain to his father and weep over her divorce, and remind his father of the love of his youth, as it says (ibid. 54:6), "and a wife of youth, when she is rejected" - and through this he arouses the love of Tiferet toward her, and the children are obligated to arouse this love in their prayer. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 56, in the gloss): woe to those people whose hearts and eyes are sealed, who do not strive to know the honor of their Master, to appease Him with the Shechinah through several supplications and appeasements, to bring Him down to the Shechinah - and all the more so to arouse love toward her, as they instituted, "who chooses His people Israel in love" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:77: Further, it explains in the Tikkunim (page 35a) that the Shechinah is the one who guards us in every place, and therefore Israel are obligated to unify her in their commandments and prayer; in these words: happy is Israel, whose feet accompany the Shechinah, to stand with her whether in ease or in distress - for when they are in judgment, on the day of judgment, which is Rosh Hashanah, she stands with them for judgment, for they establish her through their prayers, of whom it is said (Proverbs 6:22), "when you walk, it shall lead you; when you sleep, it shall watch over you; and when you awake, it shall talk with you" - for in every place Israel stand, in every single commandment, for the Shechinah, she stands for them in every difficulty and distress, whether on the road, or in a settlement, or at sea - and this is "when you walk," from the wilderness, "it shall lead you" - this is what is written (Psalms 85:14), "righteousness shall go before Him, and shall set his footsteps on the way." "When you sleep," in a settlement, "it shall watch over you"; "and when you awake," to descend to the sea, "it shall talk with you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:78: And behold, of a glimpse of this love, Rashbi, peace be upon him, says there (Zohar, Parashat Ha'azinu, beginning of page 298): it is taught, Rabbi Yehuda says, however much I have considered, the Holy One, blessed be He, has never withheld His love from Israel - for wherever they were, the Holy One, blessed be He, was among them, as it is written (Leviticus 26:44), "I have not rejected them, nor have I abhorred them, to destroy them utterly, to break My covenant with them" - precisely "with them," among them, with them - He never departs from them, forever. Rabbi Yitzchak was walking on the road, and Rabbi Chiya met him. He said to him: I see in your face that your dwelling is in the dwelling of the Shechinah. What is written (Exodus 3:8)? "And I have come down to deliver him out of the hand of the Egyptians" - "and I have come down" - it should have said "I will come down"; "and I have come down" first - when? When Jacob descended to Egypt - and why? "To deliver him out of the hand of the Egyptians" - for were it [the Shechinah] not among them, they could not have borne the exile - meaning, "I am with him in distress; I will deliver him and honor him" (Psalms 91:15). He said to him: certainly, in every place Israel dwell, the Holy One, blessed be He, is among them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:79: Further, there: Rabbi Chiya said, it is written (Isaiah 49:15), "can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?" - this verse has already been established [elsewhere], but what does it speak of here? Come and see, thus said Rabbi Elazar in the name of his father: Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He, from the day we fell into exile, the Holy One, blessed be He, has left us in exile and forgotten us - this is what is written (Isaiah 49:14), "but Zion said, the LORD has forsaken me, and my Lord has forgotten me." The Shechinah said, "can a woman forget her nursing child" - are not Israel called "children," as it is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children of the LORD your God" - "the son of her womb," as it says (Jeremiah 2:21), "yet I had planted you a noble vine, wholly a true seed" - "even these may be forgotten" - as it is written (Genesis 2:4), "these are the generations of the heavens and the earth" - "yet I will not forget you" - from here, that the Holy One, blessed be He, never forsakes Israel. Further, he says: "can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb" - this is a supernal secret that the Holy One, blessed be He, speaks - for these matters are held within His Name; just as the Holy One, blessed be He, does not forget His own Name, for He is everything, so the Holy One, blessed be He, does not forget Israel, who are literally held within His Name - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:80: And since Israel are called children and are held within His Name, it is fitting that they act as children act, in the manner of honoring their father - and so they explain in the Midrash, Eleh HaDevarim Rabbah, Parashat Ki Tavo, on the verse "and Moses called to all Israel," in these words: another interpretation (Proverbs 2:1), "my son, if you receive my words" - Rabbi Yehuda bar Shalom said, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: when are you called My sons? When you receive My words. To what may this be compared? To a king whose son said to him, "designate me within the province, that I am your son." His father said to him: do you wish that all know that you are my son? Wear my purple robe and put my crown on your head, and all will know that you are my son. So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: do you wish to be designated as My sons? Occupy yourselves with Torah and commandments, and all will see that you are My sons - to this point. And what is said in the allegory, "purple robe" and "crown" - the purple robe is the commandments, which are a garment for the soul, and the crown is the Torah - and we will elaborate on this reason in its place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:81: Further, there: another interpretation, when are you My sons? When you receive My words. Rabbi [Yehuda] said: when Israel were in the wilderness, the pillar of cloud went before them, and the smoke of the arrangement [of the altar] and the smoke of the incense would rise, and two sparks of fire would go forth from between the two staves of the Ark and burn the snakes and scorpions before them; and the nations of the world would see them and say, these are gods, for all their functioning is only through fire! Moses said to them: and all this praise that the Holy One, blessed be He, did for you was because you accepted His Torah at Mount Sinai - this is "and Moses called to all Israel, and said to them" - to this point.
